newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets up commodities data computer network.
newsitem.headline: China sets up commodities data computer network.

text.p: A computer network providing information on China's commodities markets has started operation in Beijing, the China Daily said on Thursday.

The China Commodity Market Information Network links the commodities markets in six cities -- Beijing, the northern port city of Tianjin, the southern boomtown of Shenzhen, the northeastern cities of Dalian and Changchun and the ancient city of Xian, the newspaper said.

It supplies information on 10 types of commodities -- agricultural products and their by-products, grain and edible oil, chemical products, textiles, construction materials, household electrical appliances, computers, automobiles and spare parts, China Daily said.
The network, established by the Ministry of Internal Trade, is expected to cover 14 cities by the end of the year, the newspaper said.

"The network will serve as an effective bridge between government administrative departments and markets, between producers, retailers and the country's 4,000 major wholesale markets," Deng Yongcheng, director of the ministry's market development department, said.
The newspaper gave no further details.
